response.query: Which lightweight diagnostics detect analytic propagation failure (e.g., Jacobian-weighted variance growth, calibration drift), and what thresholds trigger automatic fallback to sampling?
response.answer: Lightweight diagnostics like Jacobian-weighted variance growth and calibration drift detect analytic propagation failure, triggering automatic fallback to sampling when thresholds are exceeded. Common thresholds involve significant variance or drift beyond predefined limits.

results.title: Track: Poster Session 6
results.content: Predicting the change in binding free energy ($\Delta \Delta G$) is crucial for understanding and modulating protein-protein interactions, which are critical in drug design.Due to the scarcity of experimental $\Delta\Delta G$ data, existing methods focus on pre-training, while neglecting the importance of alignment.In this work, we propose Boltzmann Alignment technique to transfer knowledge from pre-trained inverse folding models to prediction of $\Delta\Delta G$.We begin by analyzing the thermodynamic definition of $\Delta\Delta G$ and introducing the Boltzmann distribution to connect energy to the protein conformational distribution. Experimental analysis reveals that proposed approach is not only $\times 30$ faster than prior training-based methods (\*eg, textual inversion, dreambooth-lora\*) but also surpasses the prior \*state-of-the-art\*, exhibiting improved multi-character consistency and text-to-image alignment performance. To address this, we propose an effective yet efficient approach that reframes the CLIP model into a learning-to-rank task and introduces a lightweight adapter to augment CLIP for text-guided image ranking.
